messages.preview: Found it — dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `responseType` based on `T` (`T == String` → `ResponseType.plain`). Let me check for direct non-String dio usage in the repo.

blocks.text:
There it is: dio's `fetch<T>` sets `responseType = ResponseType.plain` when `T == String`. So `dio.get<String>` forces plain-text responses (no JSON decode) — data is always String. That's why production works.

Now the interceptor's replay: `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → T=String → sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain → returns String. Consistent with the original `get<String>` call. 

BUT: **it mutates `err.requestOptions.responseType`**. If a caller had used `get<Map<String, dynamic>>` (responseType json, T=Map), the original fetch set responseType=json; the 429 error's requestOptions has responseType=json; the interceptor's replay with fetch<String> overwrites responseType → **plain**. Two consequences:
1. The replayed response data is a raw String (not decoded JSON).
2. The outer assureResponse<Map<String, dynamic>> casts String → Map → **TypeError** → surfaces as DioException.unknown.

So a caller using `dio.get<Map<String,dynamic>>` on a GithubHttpClient dio would get a raw JSON string on retry instead of a parsed map, plus a type error. As demonstrated in probe 3. This is only relevant for callers that use the dio directly with non-String T. All in-repo callers use BaseHttpClient's <String> methods. But `GithubHttpClient.dio` is public and the interceptor class is exported in the public API (`lib/dmtools.dart`) — users could attach it elsewhere.

Correct approach in the interceptor: use `_dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions)` (or `fetch(requestOptions)` preserving original T semantics — dio's fetch<T> with dynamic doesn't override responseType). Since requestOptions already carries its responseType from the original call, replaying via fetch<dynamic> preserves the original behavior exactly.

Hmm wait — one nuance: with fetch<dynamic>, `T != dynamic` false → responseType untouched → the original call's T (e.g. String → plain already set on the original call... wait, the original call already mutated requestOptions.responseType to plain when it called fetch<String>). So the replay with fetch<dynamic> keeps plain → data String → outer cast to String? fine. For a get<Map<...>> original: responseType json preserved by replay → data Map → outer cast to Map fine. So fetch<dynamic> is strictly more correct.

fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.
The input folder is `input/gh-351/`. Let me read all the files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]

So real GitHub responses (content-type: application/json) WOULD be parsed into a Map, and `dio.get<String>`'s final `assureResponse<String>` cast `Map → String?` would throw a TypeError.

This is a pre-existing concern with BaseHttpClient (not this PR), BUT — wait. It matters for this PR: the interceptor's replay uses `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)`. Let me think about what happens in the retry flow with real GitHub:

1. Request 1 → 429 → `DioException.badResponse` thrown from _dispatchRequest (inner fetch — no T cast yet, the cast happens at the outermost fetch in dio_mixin line ~587).

Actually wait, I need to be careful about the two fetch calls:
- Outer: user calls `dio.get<String>` → fetch<String> (outermost). Interceptor chain wraps it.
- Inner: interceptor's `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → a full new pipeline with its own assureResponse<String> at its end.

In the inner fetch (replay): pipeline → 200 OK → dispatchRequest returns Response<dynamic> with data=Map (JSON parsed) → interceptors onResponse (none) → assureResponse<String> → `response.data as String?` → **TypeError: Map is not String**.

Then in the interceptor's `onError`... wait no, the replay happens inside the interceptor's onError via `await _dio.fetch<String>(...)`. The TypeError (not DioException) propagates: the inner fetch throws TypeError, which is NOT caught by `on DioException catch` → propagates out of the interceptor's onError → dio wraps error interceptor invocation... messages.preview: Found it — dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `responseType` based on `T` (`T == String` → `ResponseType.plain`). Let me check for direct non-String dio usage in the repo.

blocks.text:
There it is: dio's `fetch<T>` sets `responseType = ResponseType.plain` when `T == String`. So `dio.get<String>` forces plain-text responses (no JSON decode) — data is always String. That's why production works.

Now the interceptor's replay: `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → T=String → sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain → returns String. Consistent with the original `get<String>` call. 

BUT: **it mutates `err.requestOptions.responseType`**. If a caller had used `get<Map<String, dynamic>>` (responseType json, T=Map), the original fetch set responseType=json; the 429 error's requestOptions has responseType=json; the interceptor's replay with fetch<String> overwrites responseType → **plain**. Two consequences:
1. The replayed response data is a raw String (not decoded JSON).
2. The outer assureResponse<Map<String, dynamic>> casts String → Map → **TypeError** → surfaces as DioException.unknown.

So a caller using `dio.get<Map<String,dynamic>>` on a GithubHttpClient dio would get a raw JSON string on retry instead of a parsed map, plus a type error. As demonstrated in probe 3. This is only relevant for callers that use the dio directly with non-String T. All in-repo callers use BaseHttpClient's <String> methods. But `GithubHttpClient.dio` is public and the interceptor class is exported in the public API (`lib/dmtools.dart`) — users could attach it elsewhere.

Correct approach in the interceptor: use `_dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions)` (or `fetch(requestOptions)` preserving original T semantics — dio's fetch<T> with dynamic doesn't override responseType). Since requestOptions already carries its responseType from the original call, replaying via fetch<dynamic> preserves the original behavior exactly.

fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.
The input folder is `input/gh-351/`. Let me read all the files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

messages.preview: Found it — dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `responseType` based on `T` (`T == String` → `ResponseType.plain`). Let me check for direct non-String dio usage in the repo.

blocks.text:
There it is: dio's `fetch<T>` sets `responseType = ResponseType.plain` when `T == String`. So `dio.get<String>` forces plain-text responses (no JSON decode) — data is always String. That's why production works.

Now the interceptor's replay: `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → T=String → sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain → returns String. Consistent with the original `get<String>` call. 

BUT: **it mutates `err.requestOptions.responseType`**. If a caller had used `get<Map<String, dynamic>>` (responseType json, T=Map), the original fetch set responseType=json; the 429 error's requestOptions has responseType=json; the interceptor's replay with fetch<String> overwrites responseType → **plain**. Two consequences:
1. The replayed response data is a raw String (not decoded JSON).
2. The outer assureResponse<Map<String, dynamic>> casts String → Map → **TypeError** → surfaces as DioException.unknown.

fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.
The input folder is `input/gh-351/`. Let me read all the files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

Now the interceptor's replay: `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → T=String → sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain → returns String. Consistent with the original `get<String>` call.

2. The outer assureResponse<Map<String, dynamic>> casts String → Map → **TypeError** → surfaces as DioException.unknown.

Correct approach in the interceptor: use `_dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions)` (or `fetch(requestOptions)` preserving original T semantics — dio's fetch<T> with dynamic doesn't override responseType). In-repo, only Confluence clients use non-String dio types (`getUri<dynamic>`, `post<dynamic>`, `get<List<int>>`) — and those are on the Confluence dio, which doesn't have this interceptor. For GitHub, all callers go through BaseHttpClient's `<String>` methods. So the `fetch<String>` hardcode is currently consistent in-repo, but it's a latent contract trap for the exported public interceptor. IMPORTANT at most; arguably SUGGESTION. Given the interceptor is exported as public API in `lib/dmtools.dart` (and `get<List<int>>`-style usage is an established pattern in this very codebase for Confluence), I'd rate it IMPORTANT — a real correctness trap, just not triggered by current callers. Hmm — but wait: for `get<List<int>>` (ResponseType.bytes), fetch<T> skips the responseType mutation (`bytes`/`stream` skip). Replay `fetch<String>` would NOT skip (options.responseType is bytes → the outer if `!(bytes||stream)` is false → no mutation! Wait: `if (T != dynamic && !(responseType == bytes || responseType == stream))` — with T=String and responseType=bytes, the condition is `true && !(true)` = false → no mutation. So for bytes-typed requests, replay fetch<String> keeps bytes → data = Uint8List → outer cast String? → TypeError → DioException.unknown. So bytes callers break too. Only plain-String callers work.

Also `<dynamic>` callers (Confluence pattern `getUri<dynamic>`): T=dynamic → no mutation; replay `fetch<String>` → sets plain → data String → outer cast dynamic fine — data would be String instead of decoded JSON Map! Silent semantic change: retried `getUri<dynamic>` returns a raw String body instead of the parsed Map. That's a silent wrong-result, worse than a loud error. (Confluence doesn't use this interceptor though.)

OK. Now — the important remaining checks:

A. Java parity of the wiring: In Java, which client uses RetryPolicy for GitHub? The Java fix fab5b0ea is about the GitHub integration's RetryPolicy. Let me check the Java source reference... I can't clone Java repo easily (network?). Let me try fetching the commit from GitHub to verify parity claims. Actually let me try `git ls-remote` / web fetch of the commit. The AGENTS.md says the Java reference is https://github.com/epam/dm.ai. Commit fab5b0ea. Let me try web_fetch on the commit URL.

B. Whether `Retry-After` seconds jitter applies and whether cap semantics match. Already in SyncRetryPolicy (gh-318, previously reviewed presumably). The PR reuses it — fine.

C. Attempt budget semantics: Java RetryPolicy: `maxRetries` = number of retries? Java comment: "the loop runs while `attemptNumber <= maxRetries`". Java DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 5 → 5 total attempts. The interceptor: `retriesUsed >= maxAttempts - 1` → replays while retriesUsed < 4 → total attempts = 5 (1 original + 4 replays). Test expects 5 adapter calls, 4 sleeps. Matches Java (attempts ≤ maxRetries where attempt counts from 1... Java: `attemptNumber <= maxRetries` with attempt starting at 1 → 5 attempts total). OK parity.

Hmm wait — but there's a subtlety: the interceptor passes `retriesUsed + 1` as the attempt number to statusDelayMs. For the first retry, retriesUsed=0 → attempt=1 → backoff = baseDelayMs * multiplier^0 = 1s. In Java, the first retry after the initial attempt is attempt... Java loop: `while (attemptNumber <= maxRetries)` — first execution attemptNumber=1 IS the initial attempt; retry increments then delay computed for the NEXT attempt. Hmm, in Java BasicRestClient/JiraClient: on failure with attempt=1, delay = calculateDelayMs(1, headers, status)? or (2)? Depends. The SyncRetryPolicy is the established port (gh-318, reviewed before); the interceptor calling `statusDelayMs(retriesUsed + 1, ...)` matches "delay before attempt retriesUsed+2" hmm. Honestly, this level of nitpick on off-by-one jitter base is minor; the policy API was designed as `statusDelayMs(attempt, headers, statusCode)` = "Delay before the next attempt after a retryable-status [attempt] (1-based)". After the original request (attempt 1) fails, delay for next = statusDelayMs(1,...)? By the doc: "Delay before the next attempt after a retryable-status [attempt] (1-based)". So after attempt 1 fails, call statusDelayMs(1) → returns delay for attempt 2. The interceptor calls statusDelayMs(retriesUsed + 1) where retriesUsed counts completed replays. Original fails: retriesUsed=0 → statusDelayMs(1). Correct per the API doc. 

D. Budget guard `maxAttempts <= 1`: with maxAttempts=1, no replay — original passes through. OK.

E. PropertyReader override handling in tests: `PropertyReader.setOverrides` in wiringTests/capResolutionTests — with tearDown clearOverrides. Also `PropertyReader.testIsolation = true` in setUpAll. Let me look at other test files (github_test_support) for conventions.

I. Check the export ordering in lib/dmtools.dart — check surrounding exports. Already seen: github_rate_limit_retry.dart placed among github exports but file lives in `integrations/` root, not `integrations/github/`. Minor inconsistency (all other github files are in github/). Suggestion.

J. Duplication: `_rateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` duplicates SyncRetryPolicy's private static resolver + the same logic exists in fromEnvMap. A `SyncRetryPolicy.resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds(String? Function(String))` public static could be reused. IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION? It's a small pure function (6 lines), duplicated exactly. The PR explicitly documents Java parity naming. I'd call it SUGGESTION (small, stable, documented). Hmm — the review guideline says "Duplication — copy-paste, duplicated logic across files". It IS duplicated logic across files. But making the SyncRetryPolicy static public would be a trivial refactor. I'll rate SUGGESTION.

```
/// Factory wiring: interceptor attached to every GithubHttpClient transport

Clear copy-paste error. SUGGESTION.

Potential double-interceptor attach: if `GithubHttpClient(reader, dio: sharedDio)` factory is called twice with the same dio instance (e.g., integration_clients.dart it's created once; github_ticket_source.dart creates new). Each factory call adds ANOTHER interceptor to the same dio. If a caller passes the same dio to two GithubHttpClient factories, two interceptors → 429 handling doubles (each maintains its own extra counter though — both increment the same extra key! Actually both read/write the same `extra[_retryCountKey]` — first interceptor replays; replay re-enters both interceptors' onError... Since interceptor A fetches, the replay goes through the chain including A and B; the counter is shared in extra. Hmm, worst case: double sleeps? Interceptor order: A.onError sees 429, budget ok → sleeps → fetch → (chain: B.onError sees the 429 again first? No wait — the replay request goes through onRequest → dispatch → if 429 again → onError chain: B first (added later? order is registration order: A then B; onError runs A then B)... complex. Each onError call awaits sleep and fetches. This could produce more than maxAttempts total attempts. But this only happens if the same dio is injected into two factories — pathological usage, not in-repo. Skip or mention as edge note within the attach finding. Probably skip; too speculative. Could fold into the "factory mutates injected dio" suggestion.

M. More significant: **the interceptor holds `Dio _dio` and is added to that same dio's interceptors** — replay via `_dio.fetch` — standard pattern, fine.

N. **Cancellation**: if the CancelToken is cancelled during the (up to 1h!) sleep, the interceptor still sleeps the full duration then replays. The sleep isn't interruptible. fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting

- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.
The input folder is `input/gh-351/`. Let me read all the files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

**Interruptibility/cancellation during long waits**: worth a SUGGESTION — during a capped 3600s sleep, a CancelToken cancellation won't interrupt the sleep; the request future is blocked up to an hour. Java sleeps synchronously too (parity), so maybe just note. I'll include as a SUGGESTION in the interceptor comment file... Actually keep findings tight: this is parity-preserving behavior; the Java fix waits too. I'll mention it only briefly as a note in a suggestion comment (non-blocking).

Now, one more important check: **interceptor replay for requests with non-replayable `data` (Stream/FormData)**. GithubHttpClient methods (BaseHttpClient) send `body` as Object? — for post/put/patch, `data: body` where body is typically a Map or String — dio transforms at dispatch; requestOptions.data remains the original object (transformData writes to a stream but options.data unchanged? `_transformData` returns a stream; for Map data, it JSON-encodes to a String stream each call — actually `Transformer.defaultTransformRequest` produces a String; the RequestOptions.data stays the Map. On replay, _transformData re-encodes. So Map/String bodies replay fine. FormData would not, but GitHub client never sends FormData. Fine.

**Check `handle老妈`** — enough.

The export block is alphabetically ordered by path (`github/github_http_client.dart` < `github_rate_limit_retry.dart` < `github/github_tools.dart`? No — alphabetically `github/github_tools.dart` would come before `github_rate_limit_retry.dart` since '/' (0x2F) < '_' (0x5F)). So `'src/integrations/github_tools.dart'` < `'src/integrations/github_rate_limit_retry.dart'` in ASCII ordering. The current placement (between github_http_client and github_tools) is NOT sorted: correct sort would be github_client, github_http_client, github_tools, then github_rate_limit_retry. Minor nit — but is this list sorted by path or just loosely? ado/ado_client, ado/ado_http_client, ado/ado_tools, base_http_client, bearer_http_client, file/file_tools, github/github_client, github/github_http_client, [github_rate_limit_retry], github/github_tools, confluence/... — wait, confluence AFTER github? That's not alphabetical (c < f < g). So the list is NOT strictly sorted — confluence comes after github, figma after confluence... so ordering is by feature grouping/intent, not strict ASCII. Hence placement is fine and no finding.

This is the first interceptor in the codebase (no other interceptors). OK.

Now, PropertyReader.getValue at line 163 — check the chain.
