# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

messages.preview: Found it — dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `responseType` based on `T` (`T == String` → `ResponseType.plain`). Let me check for direct non-String dio usage in the repo.

blocks.text:
There it is: dio's `fetch<T>` sets `responseType = ResponseType.plain` when `T == String`. So `dio.get<String>` forces plain-text responses (no JSON decode) — data is always String. That's why production works.

Now the interceptor's replay: `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → T=String → sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain → returns String. Consistent with the original `get<String>` call. 

BUT: **it mutates `err.requestOptions.responseType`**. If a caller had used `get<Map<String, dynamic>>` (responseType json, T=Map), the original fetch set responseType=json; the 429 error's requestOptions has responseType=json; the interceptor's replay with fetch<String> overwrites responseType → **plain**. Two consequences:
1. The replayed response data is a raw String (not decoded JSON).
2. The outer assureResponse<Map<String, dynamic>> casts String → Map → **TypeError** → surfaces as DioException.unknown.

So a caller using `dio.get<Map<String,dynamic>>` on a GithubHttpClient dio would get a raw JSON string on retry instead of a parsed map, plus a type error. As demonstrated in probe 3. This is only relevant for callers that use the dio directly with non-String T. All in-repo callers use BaseHttpClient's <String> methods. But `GithubHttpClient.dio` is public and the interceptor class is exported in the public API (`lib/dmtools.dart`) — users could attach it elsewhere.

Correct approach in the interceptor: use `_dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions)` (or `fetch(requestOptions)` preserving original T semantics — dio's fetch<T> with dynamic doesn't override responseType). Since requestOptions already carries its responseType from the original call, replaying via fetch<dynamic> preserves the original behavior exactly.

Hmm wait — one nuance: with fetch<dynamic>, `T != dynamic` false → responseType untouched → the original call's T (e.g. String → plain already set on the original call... wait, the original call already mutated requestOptions.responseType to plain when it called fetch<String>). So the replay with fetch<dynamic> keeps plain → data String → outer cast to String? fine. For a get<Map<...>> original: responseType json preserved by replay → data Map → outer cast to Map fine. So fetch<dynamic> is strictly more correct.

So finding #1 (IMPORTANT): hardcoded `fetch<String>` in the replay breaks non-String response types for any direct dio user; use `fetch<dynamic>`/`fetch` to preserve the original request's response type. fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

1. Check PropertyReader.getValue chain & testIsolation for the test claims.
2. Check the `mockGithubHttp` usage in wiringTests: PropertyReader.setOverrides(_testConfig) inside mockGithubHttp — plus capResolutionTests sets overrides including RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS. tearDown(clearOverrides) handles cleanup. OK.

Also double-check the diff on `github_http_client.dart`: the factory now attaches the interceptor even when `dio` is injected by tests — `mockGithubHttp` creates fresh Dio per fixture so no double-attach. But `GithubHttpClient(PropertyReader(), dio: Dio())` in capResolutionTests creates 6+ Dio instances — fine.

One more consideration — **the `Random()` allocation in the factory**: fine.

**Potential double-retry with `receiveTimeout`?** No.

**Interruptibility/cancellation during long waits**: worth a SUGGESTION — during a capped 3600s sleep, a CancelToken cancellation won't interrupt the sleep; the request future is blocked up to an hour. Java sleeps synchronously too (parity), so maybe just note. I'll include as a SUGGESTION in the interceptor comment file... Actually keep findings tight: this is parity-preserving behavior; the Java fix waits too. I'll mention it only briefly as a note in a suggestion comment (non-blocking).

Now, one more important check: **interceptor replay for requests with non-replayable `data` (Stream/FormData)**. GithubHttpClient methods (BaseHttpClient) send `body` as Object? — for post/put/patch, `data: body` where body is typically a Map or String — dio transforms at dispatch; requestOptions.data remains the original object (transformData writes to a stream but options.data unchanged? `_transformData` returns a stream; for Map data, it JSON-encodes to a String stream each call — actually `Transformer.defaultTransformRequest` produces a String; the RequestOptions.data stays the Map. On replay, _transformData re-encodes. So Map/String bodies replay fine. FormData would not, but GitHub client never sends FormData. Fine.

**Check `handle老妈`** — enough.

PropertyReader chain confirmed as documented. Now let me think about the `_rateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` duplication once more:

- `SyncRetryPolicy._rateLimitMaxWaitSeconds(String? Function(String))` — private static, identical logic.
- `SyncRetryPolicy.fromEnvMap` calls the private one with the env lookup.
- `GithubHttpClient._rateLimitMaxWaitSeconds(PropertyReader)` duplicates the same parse+fallback logic to route through PropertyReader.

A cleaner approach: make the SyncRetryPolicy resolver public (`SyncRetryPolicy.resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds(String? Function(String) get)`) and call `SyncRetryPolicy.resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds(reader.getValue)`. That removes the duplicated parse/fallback logic. SUGGESTION-level (6 lines, stable, both documented as Java-parity).

Java difference note: Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` logs a warning on invalid values; Dart logs nothing. The codebase's property parsing helpers (`_intEnv`) also don't log — established pattern. Skip or tiny note. Skip.

Now the `fetch<String>` replay finding. Severity: IMPORTANT. Justification:
- The interceptor is public API (exported via lib/dmtools.dart).
- Hardcoded `fetch<String>` mutates `requestOptions.responseType` to `plain` for any non-String-typed caller and produces a raw String where the caller expected a decoded Map/List (silent data-shape change) or a TypeError surfaced as DioException.unknown (bytes/Map callers).
- Verified empirically: `get<Map<String,dynamic>>` + retry → DioException(unknown) with TypeError; `getUri<dynamic>`-style callers would silently get a String body.
- All current in-repo callers use `<String>` (BaseHttpClient), so nothing breaks today — hence IMPORTANT, not BLOCKING.

Fix: `handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch(err.requestOptions));` — `fetch<dynamic>`/untyped fetch leaves `requestOptions.responseType` untouched and preserves the original call's semantics exactly (the original `fetch<T>` already set the right responseType on the requestOptions before the request was dispatched). Actually careful: untyped `fetch` → T=dynamic → no mutation → replays with requestOptions.responseType as originally set (plain for String callers since original fetch<String> mutated it... wait, did the original fetch mutate requestOptions.responseType to plain? Yes — fetch<String> sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain BEFORE dispatch; err.requestOptions is the same RequestOptions object, so its responseType is already plain. Replay untyped → stays plain → String data → outer assureResponse<String> fine. For get<Map> original: responseType json → replay keeps json → Map → outer cast to Map fine. 

So the one-line fix is `handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions));` or plain `fetch(...)`. 

Second finding: duplicate doc line in the test (SUGGESTION).

Third: duplication of the cap resolver (SUGGESTION).

Fourth: file location `lib/src/integrations/github_rate_limit_retry.dart` vs `github/` package dir (SUGGESTION).

Also consider: **test asserts `Retry-After takes precedence over X-RateLimit-Reset`** — passes `f.sleeps.single, const Duration(seconds: 10)` — exact 10s despite jitter ±15%? Retry-After branch IS jittered (jittered: true). With `_policy()` using `jitterFactor: 0.3` and default random = `_NeutralRandom()` (nextDouble → 0.5 → jitter = delay*0.3*(0.5-0.5)=0). So exact 10s. OK — the fixture's default policy uses the const _NeutralRandom via `SyncRetryPolicy(...)` constructor default `random: const _NeutralRandom()`. Yes. Exact assertion valid.

Wait — one potential test-pollution issue: `capResolutionTests.interceptorWith` creates `GithubHttpClient(PropertyReader(), dio: Dio())` — never closed; fine.

And `wiringTests` end-to-end sets overrides then doesn't clear until tearDown — fine.

**Check: `budgetAndPassThroughTests` header-less 429 fallback asserts `Duration(seconds: 1)` exactly** — backoff branch is jittered with neutral random → exact 1s. OK.

Now — anything about **`maxAttempts` duplication between interceptor field and policy.maxAttempts**? The interceptor has its own `maxAttempts` field AND the policy has `maxAttempts` — two sources of truth for the budget. In the factory wiring, both are set to 5 (defaultMaxAttempts / policy not given maxAttempts... in the factory: `SyncRetryPolicy(maxAttempts: GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor.defaultMaxAttempts, ...)`. In the default constructor: `policy ?? SyncRetryPolicy(maxAttempts: maxAttempts, ...)`. But if a caller passes a custom policy with a different maxAttempts, the interceptor's separate `maxAttempts` (default 5) governs the budget — inconsistent sources. The policy's maxAttempts is otherwise used by `statusDelayMs`? No — statusDelayMs doesn't use maxAttempts (only canRetryAfter does, not called here). So the interceptor's budget is solely its own maxAttempts field. The policy.maxAttempts is unused in this flow — slight redundancy, but only affects construction defaults. Minor; fold into a suggestion? Probably skip — noise. Actually it's worth one line in the duplication/misc comment. Hmm, keep findings focused. I'll skip this one — the API allows custom policy + explicit maxAttempts; documented defaults.

**Check error-path: `await _sleep(...)` throwing** — custom sleep injection in tests doesn't throw. Production sleep = Future.delayed — doesn't throw. Skip.

**What about `handler.resolve` being called after `handler.next` in some path?** All paths return after one handler call. Good.

**Replay `onError` of OTHER interceptors**: none exist. Good.

**The `extra` counter survives `err.requestOptions` reuse** — requestOptions is the same object across replays (dio fetch clones? `dio.fetch(requestOptions)` uses the same instance — dio docs say fetch can be called with the same options). extra mutations persist. Good.

**Now — CI workflow safety**: no workflow changes. Good.

**Security**: no secrets logged. The interceptor doesn't log. `RateLimitException`? Not applicable. No security findings.

**Backward compat**: GithubHttpClient now mutates the caller-injected dio by adding an interceptor — a behavior change for injected transports (tests that count adapter calls now see retries on 429 — that's the point). Any existing tests injecting a dio that returns 429? grep for 429 in test dir to see if other suites break. The PR says full suite green; background job will confirm.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: replay hardcodes `fetch<String>` — breaks non-String response types on the shared transport**

`GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor.onError` replays the failed request with a hardcoded type argument:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions));
```

dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `requestOptions.responseType` when `T == String` (`ResponseType.plain`, see `dio_mixin.fetch`), and the final `assureResponse<String>` casts the replayed body to `String?`. `GithubHttpClient.dio` is a public field and this interceptor is exported from `lib/dmtools.dart`, so any caller that uses the GitHub transport with a different response type gets a **successful retry turned into a failure or a silent data-shape change**. Verified against this PR's code (stub adapter: 429 + `Retry-After`, then 200 `application/json`):

- `dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>(...)` on a `GithubHttpClient` transport → `DioException [unknown]` wrapping `type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'Map<String, dynamic>?'` (the retry succeeded, the caller still fails).
- `dio.get<dynamic>(...)` → returns the **raw JSON String** instead of the decoded value (the pattern used by `confluence_client_transfer.dart`/`confluence_client_java_name_tools.dart` for other clients).

Today every in-repo GitHub call goes through `BaseHttpClient`'s `<String>` methods, so nothing current breaks — but this is a latent contract trap in exported public API.

**Fix (one line):** replay with an untyped fetch so the original `RequestOptions.responseType` is left untouched and semantics are byte-identical to the original call:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions));
```

The original `fetch<T>` has already set the correct `responseType` on `err.requestOptions` before the first dispatch, so `<dynamic>` preserves it exactly.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)

dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The

(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)

   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
There it is: dio's `fetch<T>` sets `responseType = ResponseType.plain` when `T == String`. So `dio.get<String>` forces plain-text responses (no JSON decode) — data is always String. That's why production works.

Now the interceptor's replay: `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → T=String → sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain → returns String. Consistent with the original `get<String>` call. 

BUT: **it mutates `err.requestOptions.responseType`**. If a caller had used `get<Map<String, dynamic>>` (responseType json, T=Map), the original fetch set responseType=json; the 429 error's requestOptions has responseType=json; the interceptor's replay with fetch<String> overwrites responseType → **plain**. Two consequences:
1. The replayed response data is a raw String (not decoded JSON).
2. The outer assureResponse<Map<String, dynamic>> casts String → Map → **TypeError** → surfaces as DioException.unknown.

So a caller using `dio.get<Map<String,dynamic>>` on a GithubHttpClient dio would get a raw JSON string on retry instead of a parsed map, plus a type error. As demonstrated in probe 3. This is only relevant for callers that use the dio directly with non-String T. All in-repo callers use BaseHttpClient's <String> methods. But `GithubHttpClient.dio` is public and the interceptor class is exported in the public API (`lib/dmtools.dart`) — users could attach it elsewhere.

Correct approach in the interceptor: use `_dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions)` (or `fetch(requestOptions)` preserving original T semantics — dio's fetch<T> with dynamic doesn't override responseType). Since requestOptions already carries its responseType from the original call, replaying via fetch<dynamic> preserves the original behavior exactly.

Hmm wait — one nuance: with fetch<dynamic>, `T != dynamic` false → responseType untouched → the original call's T (e.g. String → plain already set on the original call... wait, the original call already mutated requestOptions.responseType to plain when it called fetch<String>). fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: replay hardcodes `fetch<String>` — breaks non-String response types on the shared transport**

`GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor.onError` replays the failed request with a hardcoded type argument:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions));
```

dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `requestOptions.responseType` when `T == String` (`ResponseType.plain`, see `dio_mixin.fetch`), and the final `assureResponse<String>` casts the replayed body to `String?`. `GithubHttpClient.dio` is a public field and this interceptor is exported from `lib/dmtools.dart`, so any caller that uses the GitHub transport with a different response type gets a **successful retry turned into a failure or a silent data-shape change**. Verified against this PR's code (stub adapter: 429 + `Retry-After`, then 200 `application/json`):

- `dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>(...)` on a `GithubHttpClient` transport → `DioException [unknown]` wrapping `type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'Map<String, dynamic>?'` (the retry succeeded, the caller still fails).
- `dio.get<dynamic>(...)` → returns the **raw JSON String** instead of the decoded value (the pattern used by `confluence_client_transfer.dart`/`confluence_client_java_name_tools.dart` for other clients).

Today every in-repo GitHub call goes through `BaseHttpClient`'s `<String>` methods, so nothing current breaks — but this is a latent contract trap in exported public API.

**Fix (one line):** replay with an untyped fetch so the original `RequestOptions.responseType` is left untouched and semantics are byte-identical to the original call:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions));
```

The original `fetch<T>` has already set the correct `responseType` on `err.requestOptions` before the first dispatch, so `<dynamic>` preserves it exactly.

On replay failure with non-DioException (e.g. TypeError from assureResponse — exactly the fetch<String> bug): propagates out of onError → dio's catchError wrapper → the interceptor chain: `_invokeCallbackDynamically` — will the uncaught async error be routed? From dio_mixin: error interceptors are wired via `future.catchError(errorInterceptorWrapper(fun))` where fun invokes the callback dynamically. If the callback throws, `errorInterceptorWrapper`'s returned future errors → the outer try/catch in fetch catches → `assureDioException(e, ...)` → DioException.unknown. Interceptors run in registration order for onError. If a caller's own error interceptor is registered before, it runs first. Fine.

exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).

unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

1. InstructionProcessor

   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |

runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory

`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
There it is: dio's `fetch<T>` sets `responseType = ResponseType.plain` when `T == String`. So `dio.get<String>` forces plain-text responses (no JSON decode) — data is always String. That's why production works.

Now the interceptor's replay: `_dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions)` → T=String → sets requestOptions.responseType = ResponseType.plain → returns String. Consistent with the original `get<String>` call. 

BUT: **it mutates `err.requestOptions.responseType`**. If a caller had used `get<Map<String, dynamic>>` (responseType json, T=Map), the original fetch set responseType=json; the 429 error's requestOptions has responseType=json; the interceptor's replay with fetch<String> overwrites responseType → **plain**. Two consequences:
1. The replayed response data is a raw String (not decoded JSON).
2. The outer assureResponse<Map<String, dynamic>> casts String → Map → **TypeError** → surfaces as DioException.unknown.

So a caller using `dio.get<Map<String,dynamic>>` on a GithubHttpClient dio would get a raw JSON string on retry instead of a parsed map, plus a type error. As demonstrated in probe 3. This is only relevant for callers that use the dio directly with non-String T. All in-repo callers use BaseHttpClient's <String> methods. But `GithubHttpClient.dio` is public and the interceptor class is exported in the public API (`lib/dmtools.dart`) — users could attach it elsewhere.

Correct approach in the interceptor: use `_dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions)` (or `fetch(requestOptions)` preserving original T semantics — dio's fetch<T> with dynamic doesn't override responseType). Since requestOptions already carries its responseType from the original call, replaying via fetch<dynamic> preserves the original behavior exactly.

fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: replay hardcodes `fetch<String>` — breaks non-String response types on the shared transport**

`GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor.onError` replays the failed request with a hardcoded type argument:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions));
```

dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `requestOptions.responseType` when `T == String` (`ResponseType.plain`, see `dio_mixin.fetch`), and the final `assureResponse<String>` casts the replayed body to `String?`. `GithubHttpClient.dio` is a public field and this interceptor is exported from `lib/dmtools.dart`, so any caller that uses the GitHub transport with a different response type gets a **successful retry turned into a failure or a silent data-shape change**. Verified against this PR's code (stub adapter: 429 + `Retry-After`, then 200 `application/json`):

- `dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>(...)` on a `GithubHttpClient` transport → `DioException [unknown]` wrapping `type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'Map<String, dynamic>?'` (the retry succeeded, the caller still fails).
- `dio.get<dynamic>(...)` → returns the **raw JSON String** instead of the decoded value (the pattern used by `confluence_client_transfer.dart`/`confluence_client_java_name_tools.dart` for other clients).

Today every in-repo GitHub call goes through `BaseHttpClient`'s `<String>` methods, so nothing current breaks — but this is a latent contract trap in exported public API.

**Fix (one line):** replay with an untyped fetch so the original `RequestOptions.responseType` is left untouched and semantics are byte-identical to the original call:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions));
```

The original `fetch<T>` has already set the correct `responseType` on `err.requestOptions` before the first dispatch, so `<dynamic>` preserves it exactly.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr

- **PR #**: 354
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/354
- **Title**: gh-351 parity: honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait (no 60s cap)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-351` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +507
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:52:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T16:09:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #351
## What changed

Ported the Java fix `fab5b0ea` (honor GitHub `X-RateLimit-Reset` wait instead of capping at 60s) onto the dio GitHub client: new `GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor` retries HTTP 429 responses after the server-mandated wait, wired into every `GithubHttpClient` transport.

### Key decisions

- Reused the existing `SyncRetryPolicy` (gh-318 port of the same Java `RetryPolicy`) for all delay math — `X-RateLimit-Reset` waits `(reset - now) + 1s` capped only at `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 3600s), never at `maxDelayMs`, never aborted; 429 `Retry-After` is honored up to the same cap; `Retry-After` keeps precedence (Java branch order).
- Wait cap resolved through `PropertyReader`'s full chain (overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → env), matching Java `resolveRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds` (invalid/`<= 0` → 3600s default).
- Implemented as a dio `Interceptor` with the Java default tuning (5 attempts, 1s base, 60s backoff cap, 2.0 multiplier, 0.3 jitter); attempt budget bounded via `RequestOptions.extra` counter; sleep injectable for tests.
- Non-429 errors pass through untouched; header-less 429s fall back to capped exponential backoff (Java parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/github/github_rate_limit_retry_test.dart
```

Full suite (3655 tests), `dart analyze`, `crap4dart check --all` + `analyze` (CRAP ≤ 8.0) all green.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[dio request] --> ADP[HttpClientAdapter]
  ADP -->|429 + X-RateLimit-Reset / Retry-After| RL[GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor]
  RL --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.statusDelayMs]
  POL -->|wait until reset, capped at RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS| SLP[sleep]
  SLP --> REPLAY[dio.fetch replay]
  REPLAY -->|200| OK[response]
  REPLAY -->|429, budget left| RL
  REPLAY -->|budget exhausted / non-429| ERR[DioException surfaces]
```

</details>

fix(networking): honor GitHub X-RateLimit-Reset wait instead of capping at 60s ([#1](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/1))

ReportGenerator crashed when the GitHub API rate limit was hit: the existing retry honored rate limits in name only — the X-RateLimit-Reset delay was capped at maxDelayMs (60s) so it never waited for the (up to hourly) reset, and the Retry-After branch hard-aborted above 300s. The limit was re-hit, maxRetries exhausted, and the RateLimitException killed the whole report, losing all already-collected data. Fix (RetryPolicy.calculateDelayMs): - X-RateLimit-Reset: wait (resetTime - now) + 1s buffer, capped at a new configurable cap RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (default 3600s, via PropertyReader), never capped by maxDelayMs and never aborted. - Retry-After on HTTP 429: honored up to the same rate-limit cap; the 300s abort is preserved for non-rate-limit transient responses (503 etc.). - New getRateLimitMaxWaitSeconds() + constructor overload. TDD (RetryPolicyTest + AbstractRestClientRetryTest): RED showed the 60s cap / 300s abort; GREEN confirms long reset waits are honored and capped at the configured max. networking + reporting packages green.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: replay hardcodes `fetch<String>` — breaks non-String response types on the shared transport**

`GithubRateLimitRetryInterceptor.onError` replays the failed request with a hardcoded type argument:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<String>(err.requestOptions));
```

dio's `fetch<T>` mutates `requestOptions.responseType` when `T == String` (`ResponseType.plain`, see `dio_mixin.fetch`), and the final `assureResponse<String>` casts the replayed body to `String?`. `GithubHttpClient.dio` is a public field and this interceptor is exported from `lib/dmtools.dart`, so any caller that uses the GitHub transport with a different response type gets a **successful retry turned into a failure or a silent data-shape change**. Verified against this PR's code (stub adapter: 429 + `Retry-After`, then 200 `application/json`):

- `dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>(...)` on a `GithubHttpClient` transport → `DioException [unknown]` wrapping `type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'Map<String, dynamic>?'` (the retry succeeded, the caller still fails).
- `dio.get<dynamic>(...)` → returns the **raw JSON String** instead of the decoded value (the pattern used by `confluence_client_transfer.dart`/`confluence_client_java_name_tools.dart` for other clients).

Today every in-repo GitHub call goes through `BaseHttpClient`'s `<String>` methods, so nothing current breaks — but this is a latent contract trap in exported public API.

**Fix (one line):** replay with an untyped fetch so the original `RequestOptions.responseType` is left untouched and semantics are byte-identical to the original call:

```dart
handler.resolve(await _dio.fetch<dynamic>(err.requestOptions));
```

The original `fetch<T>` has already set the correct `responseType` on `err.requestOptions` before the first dispatch, so `<dynamic>` preserves it exactly.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider

callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The

(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.
